"The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, an Indian tourist who fell into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur on August 23rd, has been suspended due to safety concerns. The woman was walking along a road when the pavement suddenly gave way, causing her to plunge eight meters into the ground. Despite extensive rescue efforts, searchers have only recovered her slippers.

***

The rescue operation employed various methods including tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar technology. High-pressure water jets were used to flush the underground drainage system, and excavators worked to remove debris blocking potential rescue paths.

***

* Two divers attempted to reach the victim on Thursday but were forced to retreat due to dangerous conditions before reaching an obstacle in the underground system.

***

Dr. Zaliha Mustafa, a minister in the prime minister's department, confirmed that the operation was halted primarily due to concerns about the safety and health of rescue personnel. The fire and rescue department deemed the continuation of the search "too risky" after eight days of efforts.

***

The location where the incident occurred had experienced a soil slip the previous year, according to authorities, raising questions about the stability of the area's infrastructure. Is there anything else I can help with?"
